newsitem.title: UK: U.S. rate fears batter European bourses.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rate fears batter European bourses.

text.p: European share markets took a battering on Friday after U.S. economic data revealed underlying inflationary pressures that could spark another rise in American interest rates.
Wall Street tumbled at its opening and continued under pressure, prompting major share and futures exchanges to introduce program trading curbs.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average had shed nearly 75 points by the time European closed after stronger-than-expected core March producer prices and an major upward revision to February retail sales.
London shares lost nearly one percent on the day. They got off to a buoyant start but gradually grew jittery ahead of the U.S. data, then went into full retreat in line with Wall Street.

Paris and Frankfurt also emerged from the day bruised. Germany's electronic IBIS index fell well over one percent before recovering slightly to end 0.99 percent down. France's CAC-40 index closed down 1.28 percent.

Continuing signs of a robust U.S. economy and expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve might raise interest rates next month helped to underpin the dollar in late European trade. The Fed raised rates for the first time in 14 months in March.
The dollar trimmed its gains slightly as U.S. stocks and Treasury bonds fell, but recovered to reapproach its three-year high against the German mark and 57-month high versus the yen.
"Obviously the data today is making a U.S. rate rise look a bit more likely than it did before," said Francis Breedon, foreign exchange economist at Lehman Brothers in London.
"It's a bit surprising that there hasn't been more currency reaction to that."
Since late last week the dollar has soared by 3.7 percent against the yen and 3.8 percent on the mark.
Kirit Shah, strategist at Sanwa International in London, warned the dollar's run could begin to eat into U.S. corporate earnings and erode Wall Street prices.
"If we don't get intervention from the central banks, the dollar is going to keep on rising, which has to have an impact on earnings," he said.
Sterling rode on the dollar's coattails to scale a new 4-1/2 year peak against the mark, extending its assault on a generally feeble German currency.

The pound punched through 2.80 marks for the first time since September 1992, when it was ejected from the European Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM). But against the dollar, the British currency was stable.
Sterling's gains against the mark had more to do with weakness plaguing the German currency than sterling-specific factors, said Chris Tinker, chief treasury economist at Standard Chartered.
Revived optimism that a broad-based European single currency will get off the ground on time in 1999 helped to drive the mark to new lows against other European units.
The dollar has posted a fresh high against the yen nearly every day this week -- until Friday. Analysts said U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin's visit to Asia late last week triggered the run-up.
While in Tokyo last week, Rubin expressed concern over Japan's swelling current account surplus with the United States but also said currencies should not be used as instruments of trade policy.
Japan's Ministry of Finance has repeatedly warned of possible intervention if it finds the yen's fall excessive.
Although the United States reported that wholesale prices (PPI) fell for the third month in a row in March, the picture was less benign when the often-volatile food and energy sector was excluded.
This so-called core rate, which economists believe more closely tracks inflation, rose 0.4 percent in the month after falling 0.1 percent in February.
February retail sales were revised up to 1.5 percent from 0.8 percent previously reported by the U.S. Department of Labour.
CURRENCIES AT 1600 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.7235 marks and 126.00 yen, compared with 1.7177 and 126.02 in late European trade on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS -- CLOSING INDICES
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index closed down 42.5 points at 4,2270.7.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed down 11.44 points at 3,340.05. The electronic IBIS index fell 0.99 percent, or 33.34 points, to 3,319.24.
PARIS - The CAC-40 index closed 33.41 points lower at 2,574.56.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed lower at $347.20 an ounce, compared with the London close of $347.85 on Thursday. Silver was two cents lower at $4.79.
